declaration.reason: Implement the owner-approved fail-closed REAL/TRIAL meeting deletion boundary. A meeting is REAL by default; only an administrator explicitly creating it with the exact TRIAL marker can mark it TRIAL. Environment is immutable after creation. Only administrators may delete explicitly TRIAL meetings, with all existing safeguards retained. REAL, missing, invalid, lowercase and whitespace-padded values are non-deletable.
declaration.expectedEffect: Prevent deletion or final purge of any REAL or unclassified meeting. Permit only administrator deletion of an explicitly TRIAL meeting after existing safeguards. No other portal behavior changes.
prohibitedChanges: Never delete REAL or unclassified meetings.
Do not weaken administrator authorization, legal hold, retention, pending-review or version checks.
Do not change signing, sign-in, invitations, email-link rules, SMTP, secrets, Firestore rules or production deployment.

behaviourDifferences: Only the exact TRIAL marker at creation qualifies; REAL, missing, invalid, lowercase or whitespace-padded values are non-deletable.

activeAmendment.reason: Owner-directed Live YES pathway: close the broad signed-in meeting read boundary; route list/get reads through the server-authorized Cloudflare Gateway; enforce category, initiator, participant and invitation scopes; add invitation access only after successful dispatch and revoke it on removal/reissue. This amendment covers source and test changes only; it does not authorize publication of Firestore rules or production deployment.
activeAmendment.expectedEffect: Meeting Portal reads are limited by server-enforced category/participant/invitation policy, including dispatch-before-grant and revocation behavior, while preserving existing invitation token, SMTP, signer identity, attendance, quorum, deletion, retention and audit controls.
prohibitedChanges: Do not weaken or bypass any CI, portal-protection, Firestore approval, administrator, research, data-gate, deletion, retention or audit checks.

Do not change invitation token format/hash custody, SMTP settings or credentials, secrets, environment variables, Worker bindings, signing sessions, signer identity, PDF stamping, certificates, archives or completed documents.
Do not publish Firestore rules, change Firebase claims or grant live individual permissions without the required separate approvals.
Do not deploy production resources before staging acceptance, independent review and explicit production release.
